name: connector-fsr-agentic-assistant
label: FSR Agentic Assistant
description: Chat-driven authoring of FortiSOAR playbooks. Wraps the fsr_playbooks compiler + agent loop so a widget (or any caller) can compile/validate YAML, run an LLM-driven authoring conversation, and push the result back into the platform.

fields.name: llm_provider
fields.title: LLM Provider
fields.tooltip: Which LLM backend drives the agent. 'anthropic' uses the Claude API (Anthropic API Key + Model below); 'openai' uses any OpenAI Chat Completions endpoint (OpenAI API Key + OpenAI Model + optional OpenAI Base URL); 'fortiai-proxy' uses the FortiAI gateway through the on-box connector -- no external key to supply, though inference still leaves the appliance unless FortiAI itself is deployed on-prem. All three carry identical human-in-the-loop approval gating on tier-3+ tools.
fields.description: Select the LLM backend. Fill in the matching API key / model fields for the provider you choose.

anthropic.name: anthropic_api_key
anthropic.title: Anthropic API Key
anthropic.description: API key for the Anthropic Claude API (required when LLM Provider = anthropic). Encrypted at rest by FortiSOAR; decrypted into config at execution time. Vault references supported via the standard toggle.

anthropic.name: model
anthropic.title: Model
anthropic.description: Anthropic model id (used when LLM Provider = anthropic). Defaults to Sonnet 5 -- the volume default; pick claude-opus-5 when quality matters more than cost. The agent runs a multi-step tool loop, so prefer the adaptive-thinking family (Opus 5 / Sonnet 5, the 5.5 line, and the 4.6/4.7 models): a model without reasoning plans poorly across tool calls. claude-haiku-5-5 is the low-cost option: it screens cleanly on triage, enrichment and diagnosis, so it is a good fit for high-volume triage; its one weak spot is the playbook build hand-off, which the product's duplicate-offer guard now covers, but Sonnet 5 remains the better choice when the turn mostly authors playbooks. claude-sonnet-4-5 predates adaptive thinking and is kept only for continuity (its Haiku 4.5 sibling is not offered: it failed the build hand-off every repeat). Call the list_models operation after configuring to see the live, account-specific list.

anthropic.name: anthropic_base_url
anthropic.title: Anthropic Base URL
anthropic.tooltip: Override to point at an Anthropic-compatible endpoint (corporate egress proxy or gateway). Leave as the default for the public Anthropic API.
anthropic.description: Base URL for the Anthropic API (used when LLM Provider = anthropic). Defaults to the public Anthropic API; override for a proxy/gateway.

openai.name: openai_api_key
openai.title: OpenAI API Key
openai.description: API key for the OpenAI API (required when LLM Provider = openai). Encrypted at rest by FortiSOAR; decrypted into config at execution time. Vault references supported via the standard toggle.

openai.name: openai_model
openai.title: OpenAI Model
openai.tooltip: OpenAI Chat Completions model id. Tested: gpt-5.4-mini. Supported: o4-mini.
openai.description: OpenAI model id (used when LLM Provider = openai). Defaults to gpt-5.4-mini -- a REASONING mini. The previous default, gpt-4.1-mini, was chosen on a 15/15-vs-9/15 comparison against gpt-4o, but both of those are non-reasoning models, so that result says nothing about reasoning-capable minis; the agent runs a multi-step tool loop and plans badly without reasoning. o4-mini is the cheaper reasoning alternative. Not every function-calling model can run this agent: gpt-4.1-mini scores 3/5 on the pinned routing slice (it offers a finished build through the wrong card, and stops one call short of the approval gate) and is refused at health-check time. An unlisted model is allowed with a warning -- screen it with `make matrix MODE=gate REPEAT=3` before relying on it.

openai.name: openai_base_url
openai.title: OpenAI Base URL
openai.tooltip: Override to point at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, Together, Groq, Azure OpenAI-compatible gateway). Leave as the default for OpenAI proper.
openai.description: Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint (used when LLM Provider = openai). Defaults to the public OpenAI API.

fortiai-proxy.name: fortiai_feature
fortiai-proxy.title: Reasoning Profile
fortiai-proxy.tooltip: Which FortiAI backend profile serves the agent. Blank = whatever the fortinet-fortiai-proxy connector configuration selected (the stock box ships 'Low Reasoning' = AI_MODEL_MEDIUM as its default). AI_MODEL_LARGE is the 'High Reasoning' profile and is required for Reasoning Effort.
fortiai-proxy.description: Backend profile for FortiAI (used when LLM Provider = fortiai-proxy). Leave blank to inherit the FortiAI connector configuration.

fortiai-proxy.name: fortiai_reasoning_effort
fortiai-proxy.title: Reasoning Effort
fortiai-proxy.tooltip: How much reasoning FortiAI spends per turn. Requires the AI_MODEL_LARGE profile -- setting an effort selects it automatically, because an effort against a smaller profile is rejected outright by FortiAI. Blank = the profile's own default.
fortiai-proxy.description: Reasoning depth for FortiAI (used when LLM Provider = fortiai-proxy). Implies the AI_MODEL_LARGE profile.

fields.name: simulation_mode
fields.title: Simulation Mode
fields.tooltip: When enabled, the agent's live FortiSOAR tools (run_op, list_configured_connectors, connector healthchecks) are served from built-in simulated data instead of the live platform. Use for demos/offline testing when SIEM/TI connectors are unavailable. Leave OFF for real operations.

fields.name: persona_models
fields.title: Use Persona Models
fields.tooltip: When on, a persona that names a model for this provider (for example the ZTPF authoring personas on a stronger model) runs its conversations on that model, with this configuration's key and endpoint. Turn it off when the endpoint cannot serve those models (a gateway with its own model names) or to keep every conversation on the model above.
fields.description: Let authoring personas use the stronger model they name.

fields.name: mcp_access
fields.title: Native MCP Access
fields.tooltip: 'All servers' lets the agent use every active MCP Configuration on this platform, plus any server in the Advanced Allowlist below. 'Selected servers' limits it to the servers picked under Native MCP Servers (or named in the Advanced Allowlist). Tools that change something, such as blocking an indicator or running a playbook, always need analyst approval in either mode.
fields.description: Which native-MCP servers the agent may use.

fields.name: mcp_servers
fields.title: Native MCP Servers
fields.tooltip: Used when Native MCP Access is 'Selected servers': which FortiSOAR native-MCP servers the agent may use. The list is read live from the platform's own MCP Configurations. Picking servers on a config saved before the access setting existed limits it to those servers.
fields.description: Native-MCP servers to allow under 'Selected servers'.

fields.name: mcp_tier
fields.title: Native MCP Tool Tier
fields.tooltip: Approval tier applied to the selected servers' tools. 'read_only' runs them automatically (tier 1). 'mutating' routes every call through an approval card the analyst must accept (tier 3). Use the Advanced Allowlist below for per-server or per-tool control.
fields.description: Approval tier for the selected MCP servers' tools.

fields.name: mcp_auth
fields.title: Native MCP Identity

API key.name: soar_api_key
API key.title: API Key
API key.tooltip: A FortiSOAR API key, sent as 'Authorization: API-KEY <key>'. Preferred: it is not URI-bound, so it survives the MCP gateway's verbatim replay onto downstream /api/3 calls, and it carries the key user's identity. No token minting.
API key.description: FortiSOAR API key used as the identity for native-MCP tool calls.

Service account.name: soar_username
Service account.title: Username
Service account.tooltip: FortiSOAR service-account login used to mint a short-lived bearer token for native-MCP tool calls.
Service account.description: Service-account username (bearer identity for native-MCP tools).

Service account.name: soar_password
Service account.title: Password
Service account.tooltip: Password for the service account above. Used only to mint a short-lived bearer token against the localhost MCP gateway.
Service account.description: Service-account password (bearer-token mint for native-MCP tools).

fields.tooltip: How the agent authenticates to native-MCP servers. The built-in HMAC identity is signed for the /mcp/ URI and is NOT forwardable, so servers that fetch records or trigger playbooks downstream (e.g. SOC Framework) return 401 with it. Choose API key or Service account for those.
fields.description: Identity used for native-MCP tool calls.

fields.name: mcp_allowlist
fields.title: Advanced MCP Allowlist (optional JSON)
fields.tooltip: Optional escape hatch for per-server or per-tool control, and for servers not listed above (e.g. 'connector:<name>'). JSON object mapping a server key to {"tools": ["..."] | "*", "tier": "read_only" | "mutating"}. When set, this REPLACES the Native MCP Servers / Tool Tier selection above. Example: {"soc": {"tools": "*", "tier": "read_only"}}
fields.description: Optional JSON allowlist. Overrides the server/tier pickers above when set.

fields.name: notify_unattended
fields.title: Notify On Unattended Runs
fields.tooltip: When on, an unattended run (a scheduled hunt or auto-triage) that ends on a true positive or suspicious verdict, or that needs a person, sends one notification through the first configured channel (email, Slack or Teams). A shift summary is sent when asked for. Off by default.
fields.description: Send one notification when an unattended run needs attention.

fields.name: notification_recipient
fields.title: Notification Recipient
fields.tooltip: Email address, or Slack channel, that receives the notifications above.
fields.description: Who is notified (email address or channel).

fields.name: redaction_mode
fields.title: Model Provider Redaction
fields.tooltip: Masks sensitive values before any text is sent to the model provider, and restores them in what the analyst sees and in the tool calls the agent makes. 'off' sends text unchanged. 'standard' masks IP addresses, email addresses, usernames, hostnames, MAC addresses and secrets such as API keys and passwords. 'strict' also masks the record fields named in Redacted Free-Text Fields. The model sees stable typed placeholders (for example <IP_1>), so it can still tell that two mentions are the same host. Applies to every model call: chat turns, scope declaration, playbook building and summaries.
fields.description: Mask sensitive values before they reach the model provider.

fields.name: redaction_free_text_fields
fields.title: Redacted Free-Text Fields (strict mode)
fields.tooltip: Comma-separated record field names whose whole value is masked when Model Provider Redaction is 'strict', for example description,notes. Only the fields named here are masked as free text.
fields.description: Free-text record fields to mask in strict mode.

fields.name: reviewer_roles
fields.title: Reviewer Roles (optional)
fields.tooltip: Comma-separated FortiSOAR role names allowed to approve or reject actions and close escalations from the review queue. Leave empty to let anyone decide. When set, an analyst can still decide the actions in their own chat; everything else needs one of these roles.
fields.description: Roles that may decide approvals and escalations for other people.

operations.title: Echo Param Types (diagnostic)

parameters.title: p_text

operations.title: List Models
operations.description: List Claude models available to the configured Anthropic API key. Drives the connector configuration's Model dropdown via apiOperation. Hidden from the playbook palette — it's a UI helper, not an authoring tool.

operations.title: Warmup Reference Catalog
operations.description: Populate connectors/operations/operation_params/op_safety from FortiSOAR's /api/3/connectors/ catalog. The slim build ships these tables empty; warmup fills them at first run. Idempotent — re-running on a populated DB is a no-op unless force=true.

parameters.name: force
parameters.title: Force
parameters.description: Repopulate even if the catalog already has rows.

operations.title: Compile YAML
operations.description: Compile a friendly-YAML playbook to FortiSOAR WorkflowCollection JSON.

parameters.name: yaml
parameters.title: YAML
parameters.description: Friendly-YAML playbook source.

operations.title: Validate YAML
operations.description: Validate friendly-YAML without emitting JSON. Returns structured errors.

parameters.name: yaml
parameters.title: YAML
parameters.description: Friendly-YAML playbook source.

operations.title: Resolve YAML
operations.description: Run the resolver pass only — returns the IR with picklists/connector args resolved but no FSR JSON emission.

parameters.name: yaml
parameters.title: YAML
parameters.description: Friendly-YAML playbook source.

operations.title: Chat Turn
operations.description: Run one turn of the LLM-driven playbook authoring loop. Stub in 0.0.1; full implementation lands when storage + agent wiring is complete.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: Stable identifier the widget passes per chat session.

parameters.name: intent
parameters.title: Intent
parameters.description: Task intent discriminator: 'triage' (incident-response containment, biased to find_connector/find_operation/run_op with emit_action_card on mutating ops) or 'build' (playbook authoring, default). Selects the system prompt + tool slice; the user's message text is carried in messages[]. A non-discriminator string is accepted as the legacy user-message shape and defaults the intent to 'build'.

parameters.name: messages
parameters.title: Messages
parameters.description: Conversation turns (wire-form {role, content}). Carries the latest user message (and, on a triage->build handoff, the full triage transcript + directive). Omit on the very first turn only when the user text is passed via the legacy intent field.

operations.title: Chat Cancel
operations.description: Stop the session's running chat turn (C6). Marks the turn cancelled: the agent runs no further model round and dispatches no tool, and the turn ends as stopped_by_analyst. Returns cancelled=false when no turn is running.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: The chat session whose running turn to stop.

operations.title: Monitor Cases
operations.description: The Monitor's read side for the cases the assistant triaged on its own. view=list: the handled-cases queue (one row per case: verdict, confidence, where it looked, what it did or would have done, when, a handled / needs_you / reopened bucket, and the analyst feedback), filtered by bucket and time window, newest first, capped with a total. view=kpis: outcome counts and analyst agreement. view=policy: per rule, a ready-to-enforce flag with its inputs. view=tuning: per detection rule, reopen rate and a safe-to-tune flag. view=would_help: the missing or failing sources ranked by how many uncertain cases each would have helped. Read only.

parameters.name: view
parameters.title: View
parameters.description: Which view to return.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.title: Bucket
parameters.description: list only: which cases to show.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.title: Hours
parameters.description: Look-back window in hours (default 24 for list and kpis, 336 for policy and tuning).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.title: Limit
parameters.description: list only: most rows to return (default 50, max 200).

parameters.name: check_reopened
parameters.title: Check Reopened
parameters.description: Read each auto-closed record to spot one that is open again.

operations.title: Monitor Feedback
operations.description: Record an analyst's right or wrong, with an optional short note, on the assistant's decision for one record. One answer per record and analyst; a later one replaces it, an empty rating clears it. Returns the stored feedback read back with the decision's totals.

parameters.name: record
parameters.title: Record
parameters.description: The record IRI the decision was made on, such as /api/3/alerts/<uuid>.

parameters.name: rating
parameters.title: Rating
parameters.description: right or wrong; empty clears your earlier answer.

parameters.name: note
parameters.title: Note
parameters.description: A short reason (up to 500 characters).

operations.title: List Hunts
operations.description: The saved scheduled hunts: each with its question, its schedule in words, whether it is paused, its last run and outcome, the case its findings go to, and its recent runs. Read only; nothing is run.

operations.title: Save Hunt
operations.description: Create or edit a scheduled hunt: a question the assistant investigates unattended on FortiSOAR's own scheduler. A run that finds something opens a case (or comments on the open one); a quiet run is only recorded. Containment is never automatic. An omitted field keeps its value; enabled false pauses the schedule.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: The hunt's name (no colon or slash).

parameters.name: question
parameters.title: Question
parameters.description: What to hunt for, in plain words.

parameters.name: cron
parameters.title: Schedule (cron)
parameters.description: 5-field cron expression; not more often than every 15 minutes.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.title: Timezone
parameters.description: IANA timezone the schedule runs in.

parameters.name: module
parameters.title: Case module
parameters.description: Where a finding opens its case.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.title: Enabled
parameters.description: Unchecked pauses the schedule.

parameters.name: agent_config
parameters.title: Agent Config
parameters.description: The connector configuration the runner calls (default: this connector's default configuration).

operations.title: Delete Hunt
operations.description: Delete a scheduled hunt: its scheduler row, its runner playbook, its definition and its run history. Cases the hunt already opened stay.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: The hunt to delete.

operations.title: Run Hunt
operations.description: Run one hunt: an unattended investigation of its question. Called by the hunt's runner playbook on each schedule fire. With trigger set, asks the scheduler to fire it now instead. A confirmed or suspicious verdict opens or updates a case; any containment it proposes waits for an analyst.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: The hunt to run.

parameters.name: trigger
parameters.title: Trigger
parameters.description: Ask the scheduler to fire the hunt now instead of running it inline.

operations.title: Shift Summary
operations.description: An end-of-shift digest for a time window: what the assistant handled, what is waiting for a human, the notable verdicts, the sources that would have helped most and what the scheduled hunts found. Every number comes from stored data; the same digest is returned as plain text. Read only.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.title: Hours
parameters.description: Window length in hours (default 8).

parameters.name: until
parameters.title: Until
parameters.description: End of the window as epoch seconds (default now).

parameters.name: notify
parameters.title: Send as notification
parameters.description: Also send the summary through the configured notification channel. Needs Notify On Unattended Runs to be on.

operations.title: Export Audit
operations.description: Export the agent audit for a time window: sessions, model turns, tool calls, approval decisions (what was proposed, who decided, what ran) and the notifications sent, as JSON and as a flat CSV timeline. When Model Provider Redaction is on, the exported content is masked the same way. Read only.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.title: Hours
parameters.description: Window length in hours (default 24).

parameters.name: until
parameters.title: Until
parameters.description: End of the window as epoch seconds (default now).

parameters.name: format
parameters.title: Format
parameters.description: Which renderings to return.

operations.title: Playbook Health
operations.description: Run health for the playbooks the assistant bottled: per playbook, run and failure counts, failures since the last success, and the most recent failure with its failing step (via why_did_playbook_fail). Read only; nothing is run or changed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.title: Limit
parameters.description: How many bottled playbooks to list, newest first (default 20, max 50).

operations.title: Chat Poll
operations.description: Poll the streaming progress feed for an in-flight chat_turn (contract 2.5.0). Cheap read-only op (no LLM round-trip): returns event frames with cursor greater than the caller's last-seen cursor, a new cursor watermark, and a 'done' flag with the envelope stop_reason once the turn finishes. Call in parallel with chat_turn on a short interval to render incremental updates.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: The chat session whose current (highest) turn to poll.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.title: Cursor
parameters.description: Last cursor the caller has seen; 0 (default) starts from the beginning of the current turn. Pass back the 'cursor' value returned by the previous poll.

operations.title: Chat Resume
operations.description: Resume a chat turn that paused on an HITL approval gate.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: Stable session identifier (the same one passed to chat_turn).

parameters.name: decision
parameters.title: Decision
parameters.description: approve/reject an action_card, or 'choice' to answer a choice_card.

parameters.name: card_id
parameters.title: Card ID
parameters.description: Id of the action_card being approved/rejected (contract resume key for awaiting_action_card).

parameters.name: choice_id
parameters.title: Choice ID
parameters.description: Id of the choice_card being answered (with `value`).

parameters.name: args
parameters.title: Args
parameters.description: Final (possibly user-edited) arguments for an approved action_card. Defaults to the card's proposed args when omitted.

parameters.name: value
parameters.title: Value
parameters.description: Selected value for a choice_card resume.

parameters.name: approval_id
parameters.title: Approval ID
parameters.description: Legacy tier-3 gate id from a prior ApprovalRequestEvent (only the legacy approval_request surface uses this; action_cards resume by card_id).

parameters.name: note
parameters.title: Note
parameters.description: Optional reviewer note attached to the decision.

parameters.name: remember
parameters.title: Always Allow
parameters.description: With an approve on a playbook-run card that offers it: also let this persona run that playbook without asking next time.

operations.title: Respond Manual Input
operations.description: Submit a user's manual-input field values for a manual_input card. Forwards to the paused FortiSOAR workflow run (best-effort) and resumes the agent conversation so the chat narrates the result.

parameters.name: input_id
parameters.title: Input ID
parameters.description: The id of the manual_input card being responded to.

parameters.name: workflow_run_iri
parameters.title: Workflow Run IRI
parameters.description: IRI of the paused workflow run to resume.

parameters.name: decision
parameters.title: Decision
parameters.description: Approve (submit values) or reject the gate.

parameters.name: values
parameters.title: Values
parameters.description: Submitted field values keyed by field name.

parameters.name: option
parameters.title: Option
parameters.description: The button the analyst pressed, by its label (for a gate with several buttons). Absent: approve picks the primary button, reject the first other one.

operations.title: Chat History
operations.description: Return prior turns for a session from the connector's history store. Stub in 0.0.1.

operations.title: Resolve Persona
operations.description: Resolve the Key Store assistant persona (fsr_assistant_profile:<module>) UI framing for a mounted module. Fallback for the widget when the in-browser /api/3 Key Store read is 403-gated, and resolves bind_modules personas. Returns {found, module, label, ui}.

operations.title: List Sessions
operations.description: List stored conversations newest-first for the history browser.

operations.title: Rate Session
operations.description: Record an analyst thumbs up/down on a session (for triage). Empty rating clears it.

operations.title: Push Playbook
operations.description: Create a WorkflowCollection: POST the unwrapped collection to /api/3/workflow_collections via integrations.crudhub.make_request. By default replaces any existing collection/workflows with the same (deterministic) uuids — hard-deleting them first, incl. the recycle bin — then creates. Returns {collection_uuid, workflow_uuids[]}.

parameters.name: workflow_json
parameters.title: Workflow JSON
parameters.description: Compiled WorkflowCollection from compile_yaml (export wrap or unwrapped collection both accepted).

parameters.name: overwrite
parameters.title: Overwrite Existing
parameters.description: When true (default), hard-delete any existing collection/workflows with the same uuids (incl. recycle bin) before creating, so re-pushing a same-named playbook replaces it instead of 409-conflicting. Set false for strict create.

operations.title: Update Playbook
operations.description: Modify an EXISTING playbook in place — the modify counterpart of push_playbook (create-only). Snapshots the playbook into its Versions tab first and FAILS CLOSED if it cannot: no restore point, no edit. Then PUTs the compiled workflow to /api/3/workflows/<uuid>?$relationships=true&$versions=true — the playbook designer's own Save path, and the only path (an import_jobs merge_replace fallback was removed: live on 8.0 it returned ok while applying nothing, turning a failed edit into a phantom success). Returns {ok, workflow_iri, workflow_uuid, method, version_uuid}.

parameters.name: workflow_json
parameters.title: Workflow JSON
parameters.description: Compiled WorkflowCollection from compile_yaml (export wrap or unwrapped collection both accepted). The first workflow is updated in place.

parameters.name: workflow_iri
parameters.title: Workflow IRI
parameters.description: The existing playbook's IRI (/api/3/workflows/<uuid>). The widget seeds this from the open playbook in the designer. Either workflow_iri or workflow_uuid must be supplied.

parameters.name: workflow_uuid
parameters.title: Workflow UUID
parameters.description: The existing playbook's uuid (derived from workflow_iri when only the IRI is supplied).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: Labels the pre-edit restore point ("ai-pre-edit <session_id>") so a snapshot in the Versions tab is attributable to the chat that caused it. Optional.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.title: Stage in the Designer
parameters.description: Take the restore point and run every guard, then return the save body instead of writing it, for the open designer to load as unsaved changes. The analyst's own Save is the write.

operations.title: Decompile Playbook
operations.description: Read an EXISTING playbook off the box and return it as authored-style YAML — the READ counterpart of compile_yaml, in the same dialect, so the read → edit → compile → update round-trip closes. The widget calls this when the playbook designer mounts and seeds the result as the open playbook's YAML, so the assistant can see what it is being asked to edit (nothing in the build tool slice can fetch a live playbook). Returns {ok, yaml, workflow_iri, workflow_uuid, name}.

parameters.name: workflow_iri
parameters.title: Workflow IRI
parameters.description: The playbook's IRI (/api/3/workflows/<uuid>). The widget seeds this from the open playbook in the designer. Either workflow_iri or workflow_uuid must be supplied.

parameters.name: workflow_uuid
parameters.title: Workflow UUID
parameters.description: The playbook's uuid (derived from workflow_iri when only the IRI is supplied).

operations.title: Dry-Run Playbook
operations.description: Push a compiled WorkflowCollection, trigger one playbook, poll until terminal, and (optionally) hard-purge. Useful for end-to-end smoke checks from a widget.

parameters.name: workflow_json
parameters.title: Workflow JSON
parameters.description: Compiled WorkflowCollection from compile_yaml.

parameters.name: playbook_name
parameters.title: Playbook Name
parameters.description: Which workflow in the collection to trigger. Defaults to the first one.

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.title: Inputs
parameters.description: Trigger params; mapped to vars.input.params.* in the run.

parameters.name: timeout_s
parameters.title: Timeout (s)
parameters.description: Max seconds to poll the run before giving up.

parameters.name: cleanup
parameters.title: Cleanup
parameters.description: Hard-purge the pushed collection after the run.

parameters.name: use_mock_output
parameters.title: Use Mock Output
parameters.description: Run with each step's arguments.mock_result instead of live external calls.

operations.title: Render Jinja
operations.description: Render a Jinja template through FortiSOAR's own Jinja engine (so FSR-custom filters work). Optionally pass a context dict and/or a workflow execution PK/task_id to seed vars.steps.* from a prior run.

parameters.name: template
parameters.title: Template
parameters.description: Jinja source — e.g. "{{ vars.steps.Get_org.records[0].id }}".

parameters.name: context
parameters.title: Context
parameters.description: Variable bindings (e.g. {"value": [1, 2, 3]}). Merged on top of any from_pb_execution vars.

parameters.name: from_pb_execution
parameters.title: From Playbook Execution
parameters.description: Workflow PK (digits) or task_id UUID. Loads the run's vars as the base context.

operations.title: Query Reference Store
operations.description: Run a read-only SELECT against the connector's fsr_reference.db (sqlite). Useful for diagnosing what ops/connectors are in the local cache. SELECT only — write statements are rejected.

parameters.name: sql
parameters.title: SQL
parameters.description: A SELECT statement to run against fsr_reference.db.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.title: Row Limit
parameters.description: Max rows to return (default 200, max 1000).

operations.title: Get Session Trace (debug)
operations.description: DEBUG/smoke: return the recorded skill trace for a session and the deterministically-compiled playbook built from it (same build the playbook-offer accept runs). Read-only.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Playbook Name
parameters.description: Name used when compiling the trace into a playbook (default 'Triage Playbook').

operations.title: Call MCP Tool
operations.description: Invoke any of the connector's MCP tools by name and return the result. Lets playbooks call tools like find_containment_actions, list_configured_connectors, or run_op directly without going through the AI chat loop.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.title: Tool Name
parameters.description: MCP tool name, e.g. find_containment_actions, list_configured_connectors, run_op.

parameters.name: args
parameters.title: Arguments
parameters.description: Tool arguments as a JSON object, e.g. {"target_type": "ip", "probe": true}.

operations.title: List MCP Tools
operations.description: List all MCP tools registered on this connector, with names and descriptions.

operations.title: List Agent Tools
operations.description: List the agentic tool surface the LLM is handed, per intent (triage/build) and optional mounted-module persona, as a real turn on this box would advertise it. Each tool carries its approval tier, confirm_mode, source (safe / mcp:<server> / widget) and description. Set include_mcp to materialize native-MCP-gateway tools; verbose to include input schemas. Read-only.

parameters.name: intent
parameters.title: Intent
parameters.description: triage | build | both (default)

parameters.name: module
parameters.title: Module
parameters.description: Optional mounted module - applies its Key Store persona slice.

parameters.name: include_mcp
parameters.title: Include MCP Tools
parameters.description: Materialize native-MCP-gateway tools from the connector's mcp_allowlist.

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.title: Verbose
parameters.description: Include each tool's input_schema.

parameters.name: reach_servers
parameters.title: Reach Servers
parameters.description: M2.1: MCP server keys to union into the module's default surface (preview an on-ask reach). Comma/JSON list.

operations.title: List MCP Servers
operations.description: Enumerate the materialized external MCP servers and their tools, annotated with whether each server is on a given page's (module's) default surface. Answers 'what MCP is connected, and what does this page surface?' for operators wiring mcp_allowlist and for verifying M2 per-page surfacing. An off-surface server is still reachable on-ask. Read-only.

parameters.name: module
parameters.title: Module
parameters.description: Optional mounted module - annotate each server's on/off-surface status for that page.

parameters.name: reach_servers
parameters.title: Reach Servers
parameters.description: Server keys to union into the module's default surface before annotating (preview an on-ask reach). Comma/JSON list.

operations.title: Probe Native MCP (diagnostic)
operations.description: Diagnostic: call the on-box native-MCP gateway adapter with this config’s creds; reports auth mode + tools + errors.

parameters.name: server
parameters.title: Server
parameters.tooltip: Native MCP server: soc/modules/playbooks/utility or connector:<name>.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.title: Tool
parameters.tooltip: Optional tool name to call (forces the downstream /api/3 replay).

parameters.name: args
parameters.title: Args
parameters.tooltip: Optional JSON args for the tool call.

parameters.name: api_key
parameters.title: API key (override)
parameters.tooltip: Diagnostic: inject a FortiSOAR API key to test api-key auth without a config write.

operations.title: Create Scheduled Agent Task
operations.description: Create a recurring agent task: generates a runner playbook (SetVariable prompt/intent + Connectors chat_turn), pushes it, and creates a FortiSOAR scheduler row (django-celery-beat). The task definition (prompt, intent) is the intuitive handle; the schedule is the plumbing. Idempotent on name (updates if it exists).

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: Task name (the stable lookup key).

parameters.name: cron
parameters.title: Cron
parameters.description: 5-field cron: minute hour day_of_month month_of_year day_of_week (e.g. '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays 09:00).

parameters.name: intent
parameters.title: Intent
parameters.description: triage (read-only, default) or build. Scheduled tasks are almost always triage.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.title: What the agent does
parameters.description: The prompt the agent runs at each interval -- the intuitive mapping to what the task does.

parameters.name: agent_config
parameters.title: Agent config
parameters.description: Connector config name the runner invokes (e.g. fsrpb-anthropic).

parameters.name: allow_mutating
parameters.title: Allow mutating actions
parameters.description: If on, a headless run may auto-approve an action card; off (default) parks + notifies on a HITL gate.

parameters.name: notify_target
parameters.title: Notify target
parameters.description: Recipient for findings: email address (SMTP), Slack channel, or Teams webhook URL (optional). If set, the run's verdict is sent to this target via the highest-priority configured connector.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.title: Timezone
parameters.description: IANA timezone for the crontab.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.title: Enabled
parameters.description: Create the schedule enabled.

operations.title: List Scheduled Agent Tasks
operations.description: List scheduled agent task definitions, joined with live scheduler state (last_run_at, total_run_count, enabled). Pure read.

operations.title: Get Scheduled Agent Task
operations.description: One task definition + its live scheduler state.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: Task name.

operations.title: Update Scheduled Agent Task
operations.description: Update a task's cron / intent / prompt / enabled. Recompiles the runner when prompt/intent change and get_or_create-updates the schedule. Omitted fields keep their current value.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: Task name.

parameters.name: cron
parameters.title: Cron
parameters.description: 5-field cron expression.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.title: What the agent does
parameters.description: The prompt.

operations.title: Delete Scheduled Agent Task
operations.description: Delete the schedule row + the runner playbook collection + the task definition. Best-effort on the playbook delete.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: Task name.

operations.title: Run Scheduled Task Now
operations.description: Force-trigger a task immediately (bypasses cron; fires regardless of enabled). The trigger is async -- confirms acceptance, not completion.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Name
parameters.description: Task name.

operations.title: List Scheduled Task Runs
operations.description: List the runs (one per cron fire) of a scheduled task, newest-first. Each run shows its verdict, stop_reason, and a parked flag for HITL-gated runs resumable in chat. Pure storage read -- no scheduler transport.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Task Name
parameters.description: The scheduled task name.

operations.title: Notify Finding
operations.description: Push a scheduled task's finding to the analyst via a configured notification channel (SMTP email / Slack / Teams / SMS). Discovers what's configured on the box, formats the finding, and dispatches. Called by the runner playbook after chat_turn completes. Skips clean runs (no finding) to avoid spam.

parameters.name: name
parameters.title: Task Name
parameters.description: The scheduled task name.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: The run's session id (sched:<name>:<uuid>).

parameters.name: only_on_finding
parameters.title: Only On Finding
parameters.description: Skip notify when the run found nothing (default true).

parameters.name: verdict
parameters.title: Verdict Override
parameters.description: Explicit verdict text; when absent, reads the last assistant transcript.

parameters.name: notify_target
parameters.title: Notify Target
parameters.description: Email address / Slack channel. When blank, uses the connector's default config.

operations.title: Auto-Triage Record
operations.description: Triage one record unattended and end with a verdict. Called by the on-create playbook that Set Auto-Triage installs. Each record is triaged once; records outside the severity/source filter are skipped. Nothing is approved automatically: proposed actions wait in the approval queue.

parameters.name: record
parameters.title: Record IRI
parameters.description: The record to triage, e.g. /api/3/alerts/<uuid>.

parameters.name: severities
parameters.title: Severities
parameters.description: Triage only these severities (display text). Omitted: High and Critical. Empty list: any.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.title: Sources
parameters.description: Triage only records whose Source is one of these. Empty: any.

parameters.name: notify_target
parameters.title: Notify Target
parameters.description: Email address / channel told when the record needs a human. Blank: the channel's default, or no notification if it needs a recipient.

parameters.name: storm
parameters.title: Alert-Storm Grouping
parameters.description: Group related alerts and cap sessions: {group (default true), window_minutes (15), keys (sourceIp, destinationIp, computerName), same_name (true), max_sessions (100 per cap window, 0 = no cap), cap_window_minutes (60)}. Only the first alert of a group is triaged; later ones are noted and linked to it. Alerts over the cap are deferred, not dropped.

operations.title: Set Auto-Triage
operations.description: Install or replace the on-create playbook that auto-triages every new record of a module (alerts by default). Enabled = false keeps the playbook but deactivates it.

parameters.name: agent_config
parameters.title: Agent Configuration
parameters.description: Name of this connector's configuration the triage turns run under.

parameters.name: module
parameters.title: Module
parameters.description: Module to triage on create (default alerts).

parameters.name: severities
parameters.title: Severities
parameters.description: Triage only these severities. Omitted: High and Critical. Empty list: any.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.title: Sources
parameters.description: Triage only records whose Source is one of these. Empty: any.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.title: Enabled
parameters.description: False deactivates the trigger.

parameters.name: notify_target
parameters.title: Notify Target
parameters.description: Email address / channel told when the record needs a human. Blank: the channel's default, or no notification if it needs a recipient.

operations.title: Resolve Escalation
operations.description: Take an auto-triage escalation off the review queue as handled or dismissed. Decided once; a second answer is refused naming who resolved it. Actions still waiting in the session stay in the queue.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: The auto-triage session (auto:<module>:<uuid>).

parameters.name: card_id
parameters.title: Escalation ID
parameters.description: The escalation card id (esc_<uuid>).

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.title: Outcome
parameters.description: handled (default) or dismissed.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.title: Reviewer
parameters.description: The reviewer, {name, iri}.

operations.title: Undo Action
operations.description: Reverse an approved action card that ran, e.g. unblock an IP it blocked. The reverse operation comes from the autonomy policy rule's undo, else a built-in pair; the arguments are the ones that actually ran. Done once; a second undo is refused naming who undid it.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.title: Session ID
parameters.description: The chat or auto-triage session the card belongs to.

parameters.name: card_id
parameters.title: Card ID
parameters.description: The approved action card to reverse.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.title: Actor
parameters.description: Who is undoing, {name, iri}.

operations.title: List Agent Usage
operations.description: Per-turn usage telemetry (tokens, cost, model, intent, tool calls) from the connector store. Powers the monitor widget's drill-downs.

operations.title: Get Usage Summary
operations.description: Aggregated usage buckets for the charts (usage/tokens/cost over time).

operations.title: List Pending (HITL-parked) Tasks
operations.description: HITL-parked sessions awaiting an analyst (action cards / approvals paused mid-turn). Powers the monitor's 'pending tasks' panel with a resume deep-link.

operations.title: List Shadow Decisions
operations.description: The autonomy policy's shadow table: for each rule, how often it would have acted (or not) next to what the reviewer actually decided. Would-act but rejected is the number that must stay zero before a rule is enforced. Nothing is enforced in this version.

parameters.title: Since (hours)
parameters.name: since_hours
parameters.tooltip: How far back to count. Default two weeks, the shadow period required before enforcing a rule.

operations.title: Get Autonomy Policy
operations.description: The current autonomy policy document (read fresh, past the cache) plus whether it parses against the policy model. Feeds the Monitor's policy editor.

operations.title: Set Autonomy Policy
operations.description: Validate and save the autonomy policy to the Key Store. Reviewer-role gated (needs the connector's reviewer_roles set) and validated against the policy model before any write, so an invalid policy is refused and never partially applied.

parameters.title: Policy
parameters.name: policy
parameters.tooltip: The full autonomy policy document (version, enabled, mode, rules, protected).

operations.title: Get Audit Trail
operations.description: Per-LLM-call audit records (prompt, response, tokens, cost, user, status) for the auditable trail. The native /api/3/llm_activity_logs module is the canonical audit home; this op supplies the richer drill-down fields (tool calls, cache stats, tags).

operations.title: List Active Sessions
operations.description: Live agentic chat sessions with a derived status (active / waiting_approval / idle), the acting user, mounted record, latest prompt, turn count, and last activity. Powers the monitor's Live Sessions panel. Derived from the connector session stores.
